newsitem.title: GERMANY: Big shareholders want out of Salamander - paper.
newsitem.headline: Big shareholders want out of Salamander - paper.

text.p: Shareholders together owning a majority in German shoemaker Salamander AG want to dispose of their holdings due to tax changes, the Welt am Sonntag newsaper reported on Sunday.
German tax law had exempted shareholdings of between 10 and 25 percent from taxes on wealth, capital and capital trading.
But with the abolition and planned scrapping of the taxes, the holdings are losing their tax advantages, the paper said, citing informed sources.

The main shareholders in Salamander include Austria's J.M. Voith AG with 15 percent, Muenchner Rueckversicherungs AG with 13.6 percent, Victoria Lebensversicherungs AG with 12.3 percent, as well as Commerzbank AG and Deutsche Bank with 10.7 percent each.
Salamander shares ended last week at 201 marks, down six, having rallied from a low of 149 marks in January.
